 KRA Moves Individual Income Tax Filing Deadline From June to April Starting 2027 
 -->
 --> 
 by Maxwell Amunga on Tuesday, 10 November 2026 - 1:34 pm 
 An undated image of customers lining up for services at KRA's offices. 
 Photo 
 Sacco Review 
 -->
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has announced changes to the filing deadline for individual income tax returns, with the new reporting date set to April 30, effective 2027.
 In a public notice issued under its  #Elewa Finance Act 2026  campaign, the authority informed taxpayers that the current June 30 deadline will no longer apply from next year.
 “Starting 2027, the deadline for filing Individual Income Tax Returns will no longer be 30th June. The new deadline is 30th April,” KRA stated.
 KRA has since urged Kenyans to familiarise themselves with the revised filing schedule and mark their calendars to avoid missing the new deadline.
 An image of the Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi, speaking during a KRA meeting mid 2025. 
 Photo 
 KRA 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has moved the annual individual income tax filing deadline from June 30 to April 30, effective January 1, 2027. 
 The proposals were outlined under the Finance Act 2026, where salaried employees are obliged to file returns by April 30, while taxpayers submitting nil returns will face a January 31 deadline. 
 Since its inception, KRA and the National Treasury have maintained revised filing deadlines that will improve tax administration, ease congestion on the iTax platform and support faster verification. 
 KRA head for  Micro & Small Taxpayers George Obell has consistently stated the changes will also improve government revenue forecasting, reduce discrepancies in tax records and align filing processes with updated iTax dashboards and pre-filled taxpayer data. 
 With the proposal coming into effect, individual self-assessment taxpayers will be required to file by the end of the fourth month after their financial year ends. Corporate filing deadlines remain unchanged. 
 KRA has maintained penalties for late submissions, with individuals facing a fine of 5 per cent of tax due or Ksh2,000. Companies face a minimum Ksh20,000 penalty. 
 To facilitate the early tax filing plans, Commissioner Obell revealed earlier this year that the tax body intends to send every registered taxpayer a detailed pre-filled breakdown of their books starting January 1, 2027, pulling data from eTIMS invoices, withholding tax certificates, and third-party sources ahead of the April 30 sunset date.  
 Meanwhile, the tax amnesty programme runs until December 31, 2026, offering a 100 per cent waiver of penalties and interest on outstanding liabilities up to December 31, 2025, subject to payment of principal tax.
